title: Continuity of etale sections for sheaves of sets
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, let $(X_i,f_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, and let $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ with projections $f_i:X\to X_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix a stage $0\in I$ and index all subsequent stage objects and the section colimit by the cofinal upper tail $I_{\ge0}=\{i\in I:0\le i\}$. Let $G$ be a sheaf of sets on $(X_0)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Let $W_0\to X_0$ be etale and of finite presentation, put $W_i=W_0\times_{X_0}X_i$ and $W=W_0\times_{X_0}X$, and write $\rho_{i'i}:(f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)\to(f_{i'0}^{-1}G)(W_{i'})$ for the transition map obtained from the unit of inverse image, the composition isomorphism $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and restriction along the canonical iterated-fibre-product isomorphism. Then $\rho_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{i''i'}\circ\rho_{i'i}=\rho_{i''i}$, and the canonical map $$\varinjlim_i(f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)\;\longrightarrow\;(f_0^{-1}G)(W)$$ is a bijection. In particular, for the etale projection $\operatorname{pr}_i:W_i\to X_i$, restriction identifies $(\operatorname{pr}_i^{-1}f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)$ with $(f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)$.

proof.text: Apply comparison coherence to obtain the identity, transition-composition and cone-leg equations. Define E with exactly the stage section sets as objects and exactly these comparisons as maps. The first two equations give its functor laws; the third makes the cone comparisons a natural transformation to the constant limit-section functor. Choose identity isomorphisms e.

Every element of the Type colimit is represented by a stage section (Mathlib Limits.Types.jointly_surjective'). If two representatives have the same image, eventual equality supplies arrows to a common later stage on which their comparisons agree. Mathlib Limits.Types.colimit_sound' identifies the colimit representatives. Conversely a limit section lifts to a stage, and colimit.ι_desc_apply identifies its colimit representative's image with the given section. Thus the canonical colimit.desc is bijective.

For an arbitrary etale object V and sheaf F, take the inverse-image restriction isomorphism rho. Naturality at the diagonal moves rho through diagonal restriction. The unit equation identifies the resulting composite with restriction along diagonal followed by the first projection, which is the identity. The evaluated rho is an isomorphism, so the unit-diagonal section map is an isomorphism and therefore bijective. Apply this to every stage base change of W0.

The affine-site colimit theorem supplies the strictified site presentation needed for the degree-zero section comparison.
The affine-site topos equivalence transports the sheaves of sets from the full etale sites to the affine sites.
Its statement is the generic section bijection for a sheaf system on a colimit of sites.
Its finite affine etale refinement is the generic finite-cover input for the qcqs descent step.

statement_change.what: The original statement uses a stage 0 and the morphisms f_{i0} for every i without choosing 0 in I or restricting to i >= 0. A general directed set has no distinguished least element; when i is not >= 0, f_{i0} is not defined. Choose a stage and use its cofinal upper tail, as in the source limit/base-change construction. This makes the intended objects well typed without requiring I to have a least element.
